subject: MAP: Performance benchmarking & close timeline — hosted/dedicated/private plan

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff + proposed eval plan for Performance benchmarking

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation, I put together a first-pass Mutual Action Plan that focuses the evaluation on the metrics you care about: latency (p50/p95), throughput (tokens/sec), TTFT (time-to-first-token), and concurrency behavior under realistic client patterns. The attached PDF is the MAP with milestones and ownership. High level: 

- Week 1 (Mar 15–19): baseline hosted run (no burst, single-region) + short smoke tests
- Week 2 (Mar 22–26): dedicated pool tests (isolation, pinning, predictable throughput)
- Week 3 (Mar 29–Apr 2): private/VPC run (network isolation, customer infra)
- Parallel: automated load test runs and scripted prompts to exercise prefix caching and KV behavior

Target test vectors: 1) short chat (avg 40 tokens), 2) long-form generation (avg 512 tokens), 3) streaming-heavy (token-at-a-time) — we’ll capture p50/p95 latency, TTFT, tokens/sec, and observed autoscale latencies.

Please confirm the following by EOD Monday: (1) desired concurrency envelope for the proof-of-concept (150 concurrent sessions vs 500?), (2) any data residency constraints for the private run, and (3) if procurement needs us to attach an SOW.

Attached: 20270312-DataCraft-MAP-v1.pdf

Thanks —
Karthik
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alice Chen <alice@datacraft.com>

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for the MAP. This looks good and timeline aligns with our internal Q2 goals. A few clarifying Qs before you start tests:

1) For TTFT: are you measuring time from request receipt at the gateway or from our client sending the first byte? We want client-perceived TTFT.
2) Concurrency: we expect spikes up to ~300 concurrent users on launch week, sustained 120–150 afterwards. Can you design the test to emulate burst patterns (300 for 5–10m, then drop to 150)?
3) For private/VPC run: we’ll need results showing that autoscale cold-starts won’t exceed X ms — what is Redwood’s typical cold-start for isolated pools?

We can host the first baseline test on Mar 18 if that works. Procurement (Bob) is looped for SOW discussion.

—Alice
Head of Platform, DataCraft

On Mon, Mar 15, 2027 at 09:08 Alice Chen <alice@datacraft.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the MAP. This looks good...

Hi Alice — thanks for the questions — answers inline and updated plan in attached loadtest-config.yaml: 

1) TTFT: we’ll report both gateway-side TTFT and client-perceived TTFT (we’ll inject a synthetic client clock). The MAP will show both columns so you can validate perceived latency.
2) Concurrency envelope: we’ll run the burst profile you described: 300 concurrent for 10m, then scale down to 150 sustained for 60m. We’ll repeat bursts 3x across the dedicated and hosted runs.
3) Autoscale cold-starts: for dedicated pools with reserved GPU capacity you should expect <200ms additional model readiness latency (not counting network). For private on-prem this depends on your infra; our private agent typically warms a reserved replica in <500ms in our tests — we’ll show empirical values.

Proposed baseline exec dates: hosted smoke test on Mar 18; dedicated on Mar 23; private on Mar 30. If these look good we’ll kick off the first load job on Mar 18 and share the results CSV the same day.

Attachments: loadtest-config.yaml

Karthik

Quick note on measurement and the harness we’ll use (see attached CSV after first run):

- Harness: k6 driver with a custom Redwood client to capture token-level timestamps (TTFT, time-to-last-token).
- Metrics captured: request_timestamp, client_ttft_ms, gateway_ttft_ms, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, tokens_per_sec, active_replicas, autoscale_delay_ms.
- Isolation check: for dedicated run we’ll pin the model to a reserved pool and record cross-tenant noise by running a silent background workload in a separate queue (to show isolation benefits).

I’ll execute the hosted smoke job on Mar 18 at 10:00 PT and push results to the Drive link. Results will include the attached 20270315-benchmark-results-summary.csv after the run.

Thanks, I ran the hosted smoke slot this afternoon as scheduled and reviewed the CSV. Initial takeaways: p95 in hosted test spikes during bursts (expected), TTFT client-perceived is ~45ms higher than gateway TTFT (we’ll need to review the client batching behavior). The dedicated preview looks promising for isolating noise. Procurement (Bob) will prepare a short SOW and likely target the dedicated reserved offer Mar 23–Apr 23 as the pilot.

Next steps: 1) Please share the dedicated test config and exact start time for Mar 23; 2) Marissa — include the short-term reserved pricing appendix in MAP; 3) Karthik/Neha — capture autoscale cold-start samples during the dedicated run.

Looking forward —
Alice
